# WO-2026-08-15-04 — BUILD-006 Phase 3: Scribe and the Master Story Package

**The spine continues.** Phase 1 makes a real seed; Phase 2 compiles it into a real evidence pack; Phase 3
turns that pack into something a human would publish. **You consume a REAL pack produced by Phase 2 from a
REAL Phase 1 seed** — the same constraint that governed Phase 2, and for the same reason. Do not invent a
pack fixture.

## What Scribe IS, from the map §3 — read this before designing anything

> **Scribe is NOT a separate application or build. It is a persistent specialist capability within VlogOps,
> implemented as a VERSIONED CONTRACT/SKILL whose underlying model may change. Do not replace it with a
> generic one-off drafting agent.**

Its voice is **Warwick's own accumulated voice and relationship with AI**, informed by — never imitating —
Clarkson's strong premise and comic reversal, NetworkChuck's accessible enthusiasm, Simon Whistler's
structured narration. **No verbatim imitation.**

## ⚠️ THE MODEL SEAM — the central design question, and it is DELIBERATELY yours to answer

Scribe needs a language model. **You have no gateway credential and none will be granted by this order.**

The estate's precedent is `services/obsidiwikai/src/core/models.mjs` — a single seam, roles resolved to
models, refusing rather than silently substituting when `FUSION_GATEWAY_URL` is unset. **Read it. It is
the pattern, not necessarily the dependency**, and note that AsdAIr reaches it across a service boundary
which the BUILD-006 census flagged as a trap.

**What Phase 3 must deliver is the versioned CONTRACT and everything around it that is deterministic and
testable** — the prompt/skill definition and its version, the story-question and beats structure, the
Master Story Package schema, the derivation rules, the traceability, the storage, the CLI, the tests.
**The model call itself must sit behind one seam that is stubbable in tests and refuses loudly when
unconfigured.** Acceptance runs against that seam with a deterministic stub.

**⛔ Say this plainly in your return, because it is exactly the trap this estate keeps falling into: a
green suite over a stubbed model proves the CONTRACT and the PLUMBING. It does NOT prove Scribe writes in
Warwick's voice.** That is a creative judgement only Warwick can make, at Phase 5, and no test may be
presented as a substitute for it.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — It consumes a REAL pack.** Produce a real seed (Phase 1 Route 1, real window) → a real pack
(Phase 2) → a Master Story Package. State which seed and which pack id in your return.

**AC2 — ONE canonical creative truth, with siblings DERIVED from it.** The master narrative is generated
once; script, blog, titles and thumbnail direction are derived from it. **Prove derivation rather than
asserting it**: changing the master changes the siblings; a sibling cannot be generated without a master.

**AC3 — Traceability, end to end.** Every claim in every sibling carries a citation to a pack entry, and
that entry resolves. **A sibling claim that cites nothing, or cites an entry not in the pack, is refused.**
This is the criterion the whole build exists to make possible — Phase 4 verification depends on it.

**AC4 — Siblings cannot drift.** A sibling asserting something the master does not is detected and
refused. Prove it by planting one.

**AC5 — The contract is VERSIONED.** The skill/prompt definition carries a version; a package records the
version that produced it; changing the contract does not retroactively alter existing packages.

**AC6 — The model seam refuses loudly when unconfigured**, and never silently substitutes a fallback. Prove
the refusal. The `models.mjs` header records a live 400 caused by exactly that failure mode.

**AC7 — Determinism where determinism is honest.** Everything except the model's own output is
deterministic and reproducible: the same pack and the same contract version produce the same structure,
the same citations, the same package identity inputs. **Do not claim determinism over generated prose.**

**AC8 — Phases 1 and 2 still pass.** Their suites stay green on your branch. Call out explicitly any file
of theirs you change.

**AC9 — CI covers the new work** and still fails on zero executed tests.

## Required evidence

**Real output pasted beside the claims. Every exit code UNPIPED.**

- The full suite with its **executed subtest count**.
- **The AC1 chain: the real seed id, the real pack id, and the resulting package id.**
- The AC3 traceability proof and the AC4 planted-drift refusal.
- The AC6 refusal-when-unconfigured proof.
- **One real generated Master Story Package, committed as a sample**, so a human can read what this
  produces — clearly labelled as stub-model output, not as Warwick's voice.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/vlogops` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- **Any real model call, any gateway credential, any spend.** Stub the seam. `credential_scope: none`.
- **The live Supabase project.** Disposable local cluster only.
- **Phase 4 verification, Phase 5 Cockpit and approval, Phases 6–7.** Scribe produces the package; it does
  not verify it, approve it, render it or publish it. **Do not build hooks for them.**
- **Warwick's creative approval.** You cannot obtain it, simulate it, or assert his voice is achieved.
- **Phases 1 and 2's settled design.** Extend where genuinely needed and call it out; do not re-litigate.
- **BUILD-015 / AsdAIr entirely** — a separate lane with its own builders.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK, then HOLD.** Restate the outcome, your plan, what this order failed to settle, and what
   looks wrong in it — **including your proposed model seam, your Master Story Package schema, and how you
   intend to make traceability enforceable rather than advisory.** Do not implement until Larry accepts.
   **REFUSE a materially defective order** — four of my last five orders had a real defect the worker
   caught here, and that is the cheapest place to find them.
2. **Spine first:** real seed → real pack → the smallest end-to-end package with ONE sibling, before any
   hardening. Prove the chain works before you make it good.
3. Then traceability (AC3), drift refusal (AC4), the remaining siblings, versioning (AC5), the seam's
   refusal behaviour (AC6), determinism (AC7), CI (AC9).
4. **Git — worktree `C:/Fusion247PKA-vlogops3`, branch `build-006/b6-03-scribe`, cut from Phase 2's head.**
   Commit, push, open a **DRAFT PR based on `build-006/b6-02-source-compiler`** — not on main — so it shows
   only your delta and the merge order stays structural. **Do not merge. Do not touch main or either
   upstream branch. No force-push.**
5. **Return to Larry.** You do not declare Phase 3 complete: demonstration → Veritas → Codex → Warwick.
